title: New England Dream
subtitle: The work belongs to the production company, to the investors, and to the business plan, but not the author.

items.text: New England Dream

items.speaker: Newsboy
items.text: Extra, extra!

items.speaker: Newsboy
items.text: The highly anticipated movie New England Dream is about to hit the silver screen! Another masterpiece following in the grisly tradition of Nosferatu, Dracula, and The Curse of Frankenstein!

items.speaker: Newsboy
items.text: Witness the most pure and flawless vampire in film history, guaranteed to make your heart skip a beat! Behold the mysteries of an immortal race!

items.speaker: Maid
items.text: May I have a newspaper?

items.speaker: Newsboy
items.text: Fifteen cents ... Thank you, ma'am.

items.speaker: Newsboy
items.text: Today's big news: the movie New England Dream is about to premiere.

items.speaker: Newsboy
items.text: Critics have been pouring their acclaim on the film! Renowned critic Maxwell praises its intricate details and imaginative and dreamlike plot: "Director Brian Finn has once again created a masterpiece!"

items.speaker: Newsboy
items.text: The chairman of the International Illumination Film Festival lauds its aesthetic framing and composition. He cites a strong "Finn" style, which indicates Finn's active exploration of the vampire sub-genre.

items.speaker: Newsboy
items.text: "The eternally youthful image of the female lead is unforgettable."

items.speaker: Newsboy
items.text: "A Hollywood masterpiece with a quintessentially European flair!"

items.speaker: Newsboy
items.text: "The preview was a huge success, garnering rave reviews!"
*thud*
1970s, somewhere in the U.S.
*thud*
The newspaper in Brian's hand is crumpled into a ball and thrown to the floor.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: This is all wrong!

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: After the preview, I repeatedly emphasized to everyone that ...

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: ... the film absolutely cannot be released in its current state! It's still riddled with serious flaws! It needs further revision!

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: If I can't fix them, my film will never reach perfection. It'll never live up to this idea everyone has of it being some kind of "masterpiece"!
He paces the office, scratching at his increasingly sparse hair.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: But months have passed, and I haven't changed a thing.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: I have to deliver the final cut of the film today.
He paces the office, scratching at his increasingly sparse hair.
He falls dejectedly into his chair.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: What do I do? How can I present such an unfinished, fractured piece of work?
A determined look comes across his face as he shakes his head.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: No. It would be an insult to vampires! A colossal stain on my directorial career!
He stumbles to the desk and grabs the phone, the dial spinning like a whirligig.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: I must postpone it a few more weeks. Just a fortnight will do!

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: I'm sure I can find some inspiration and fix all those problems—
*knock, knock*
Before the call can connect, a visitor arrives at the office door.

items.speaker: Investor
items.text: Brian! Brian! You've been dodging us for months!

items.speaker: Investor
items.text: I know you're in there!
*bang*
The door flies off its hinges and crashes to the ground.

items.speaker: Security Guard
items.text: Sorry, Mr. Brian.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Hey! What in God's name are you doing?! You can't just break into people's property like this!

items.speaker: Investor
items.text: You know why I'm here, Mr. Bigshot Director.

items.speaker: Investor
items.text: How many times have you put off the release of this picture, pal? Do I need to remind you? Or have you come up with a new excuse?
Brian is momentarily speechless.

items.speaker: Investor
items.text: I've told you so many times that the preview went well and all the critics loved New England Dream. So what's the problem, buddy? What're you still not satisfied with?

items.speaker: Investor
items.text: There's no way this film will tarnish your reputation in any way! In fact, this'll shoot you to superstardom. You'll be huge! The next big sensation on the lips of everyone in Hollywood!

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: I don't care about any of that!

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: New England Dream is my lifelong work. It has to be flawless. It's—

items.speaker: Investor
items.text: Enough! Don't you see you're hurting everyone involved? Do you have any idea how much money we've lost to make this happen?!

items.speaker: Investor
items.text: The whole crew's livelihood is hanging on this thing! You planning on dragging them down with you?
Brian's face turns red, but he still stubbornly clings to the copy of the film in his hand.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: I understand, but New England Dream isn't ready for the big screen. We need to stop promoting it immediately, lower everyone's expectations, and apologize in the press.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Don't worry. I'll write the apology letter.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: I just need a little time to fix the problems with the film.

items.speaker: Investor
items.text: You've totally lost it, haven't you?
He waves his hand, signaling the security personnel behind him.

items.speaker: Investor
items.text: Grab the stuff. We're done waiting.

items.speaker: Security Guard
items.text: C'mon. Hand it over, Mr. Brian.
The struggle is brief.
Brian collapses to the floor.

items.speaker: Investor
items.text: The audiences, the theaters, and a boatload of investors have all been waiting for it. New England Dream is more than just your baby.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: You can't do this! This is my life's work!

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: It's not finished ...

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Give it back to me! I promise, I'll make it perfect!

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: "Sincerely, Brian Finn."
1990s, Eternity's House

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: "Sincerely, Brian Finn."

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: "Please forgive my dragging feet and hard head. It wasn't until today that I finally mustered up the courage to send you a copy of this film."

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: "Regrettably, even after twenty years, I've never been able to perfect the final edit—to find those missing pieces. It's tormented me endlessly."

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: "I hope it doesn't repulse you."

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: "Sincerely, Brian Finn."

items.speaker: Maid
items.text: What's wrong, ma'am?

items.speaker: Maid
items.text: Ever since that reel landed in your lap today, you've been all shades of blue. You even dug up that old newspaper.

items.speaker: Maid
items.text: Bless your heart, still so attached to these old things.
She carefully removes the film from the projector—the film that has traversed a great deal of time and distance to find her.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: You've kept it in fine condition. Thank you.

items.speaker: Maid
items.text: Just doing my job, ma'am. Are you sure you're okay?
The woman looks at her in the same way a worried mother looks at her child.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: It's okay. I'm fine.
She runs her fingers along the aged Persian sofa, feeling the subtle textures under her fingertips.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: So much time has passed.

items.speaker: Maid
items.text: Don't you worry, ma'am. Even though my eyes aren't what they used to be, I can still say that ...

items.speaker: Maid
items.text: ... you look wonderful. The Lord's been kind to you, that's for sure.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: I need to step out for a moment.
TO BE CONTINUED…
